title: Knowledge check: Logging and Application Monitoring

questions.prompt: In Logging and Application Monitoring, which statement best describes Structured logs?
options: Connect this syllabus point to Logging and Application Monitoring: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Normalize expected failures into safe, predictable responses and forward unexpected failures to the final error handler. Keep diagnostic details in protected logs, not public responses.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Logging and Application Monitoring?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Production readiness includes validated environment configuration, health checks, correct proxy trust, structured logs, deployment coordination, rollback plans, and incident response. A successful local run does not prove production safety.

questions.prompt: A change related to Logging and Application Monitoring appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
